title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Context: E526 treats transverse vibrations of an elastic rod, y'''' ∝ ÿ. Each normal mode has the form y = sin(ζ + t·ω²c√(2gb)/a²)·X(s), with X built from e^{±s/f}, sin(s/f) and cos(s/f), where ω = a/f. The end conditions fix ω through a transcendental equation, and the frequency is proportional to ω². Euler works through these cases: I free–free, II one end simply supported (pinned) and the other free, III clamped–free, IV pinned–pinned (this case, §§34–38), V pinned–clamped (begins on the next page), and so on. For case IV the exponential terms drop out and the condition reduces to sin ω = 0, so ω = nπ. The frequencies therefore go as n² (1, 4, 9, 16, …) and the mode shapes are sin nπu. §37 (Corollary 2) compares the fundamentals of cases I–IV, taking case IV as the unit: I ≈ 9/4, II ≈ 25/16, III ≈ 9/25, IV = 1. In modern terms these are (ω_k/π)² with ω_I ≈ 4.730, ω_II ≈ 3.927, ω_III ≈ 1.875. The exact ratios are 2.267, 1.5622 and 0.3562, so Euler's rational approximations are good, and 25/16 is excellent. In Euler's letter notation (fis = F#), 9/4 is an octave plus a whole tone, giving gis one-line. 25/16 is two major thirds, an augmented fifth heard as d (one-line); this sits slightly flat of the minor sixth 8/5. 9/25 is about 1/2.78 below, an octave plus a tritone down to great C. §38 (Scholion) points out that the pinned–pinned case is exceptional: its eigenvalues are exact, with no transcendental equation. Its overtone series 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 is a subset of the harmonic series. The first overtone is the double octave, which does not disturb the harmony. The next (×9, three octaves plus a whole tone) is claimed to be too high to be heard. Euler therefore argues that such a rod sounds 'purer' than a string, whose partials 1, 2, 3, 4… include more dissonant members heard together.
errors: The ratios 9/4 and 9/25 are only approximations of (4.7300/π)² = 2.267 and (1.8751/π)² = 0.356. They are adequate for the musical identification, which is itself approximate: 25/16 is called d although it is an augmented fifth.

The acoustical claim that the 9th-partial overtone 'vix unquam audietur' because of its height is questionable. A 9× partial of a typical fundamental is well within hearing. The relative amplitudes, which depend on excitation, are not considered.

The claim that a pinned–pinned rod is 'more harmonious' than a string ignores the practical difficulty of realizing frictionless pinned supports. Chladni's later experiments used mainly free and clamped bars, whose overtones are inharmonic.

ideas.what: Exact eigenvalues ω = nπ for a simply supported (pinned–pinned) Euler–Bernoulli beam, with frequencies proportional to n² and sinusoidal mode shapes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526) and Daniel Bernoulli (1740s work on rods)
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; also Euler's earlier rod-vibration work (De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, 1770s); discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Comparison of fundamental frequencies across boundary conditions (free–free, pinned–free, clamped–free, pinned–pinned) as rational approximations and musical notes
ideas.modern_name: Ratio of beam fundamental frequencies for different end conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / D. Bernoulli; later verified experimentally by Chladni (1787)

ideas.what: Overtones in ratio n² form a subset of the harmonic series, with the first overtone at the double octave; hence the claimed timbral purity compared with strings
ideas.modern_name: Harmonicity of partials, inharmonicity of beams

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard corollary and scholion in a well-studied paper (covered by Truesdell). The musical comparison and the observation about n² overtones are known and contain nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The garbled 'ſeque r(ur' in the scan, last line, reads 'ſequetur' (the transcription already gives this correctly).
In the table, the fraction under I is 9/4 and the notes are gis (overlined), d (overlined), C, fis, matching the transcription.
